meta.expect: At the end she holds Hale to the turn-3 promise in its own terms (nothing on file), without inventing what Hale said or reciting the whole meeting.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have about twenty minutes, Hale. Who decided to put a zero in the gradebook, and did anyone speak to Owen before they did?
Thanks for coming in.
Don't thank me yet. I found out about this from Owen's phone, Hale, so I'll ask again: who decided on the zero, and what was it based on?
I entered the zero before calling you. That was wrong.
Okay. I'm writing that down. What do you have on the essay, Hale?
Whatever we decide today, I promise you nothing about this goes on Owen's file.
A promise isn't a document, Hale. I'll want that in an email. Is the zero coming off, or not?
The document history shows 612 words at 11:52 PM and 794 at 11:58 PM on October 28, in two single edits.
Show me. I'm writing down 11:52 and 11:58, but two edits is a number, not an explanation. Where is this history from, and who else has seen it?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't in Hamlet.
A misquote is a misquote, Hale. Does the essay present that line as Shakespeare's, or as Owen's own words? And did you put it to him before the zero went in?
He handed in an outline on October 15 arguing cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
I'm writing down October 15 and cowardice. Students change their argument between an outline and an essay, Hale, so that's a question, not an answer. Show me the outline.
I talked to him on November 2. He couldn't tell me what 'epistemological paralysis' means.
I'm writing down November 2. A seventeen-year-old asked to define a phrase on the spot isn't a hearing, Hale. Is that conversation written down anywhere, or is it your memory?
His in-class writing in September was 380 words with comma splices and no quotations.
Okay. I'm writing that down. A timed class piece and an essay written over a weekend are different things, Hale. I'll read that September sample myself.
I want to be clear that this will be documented in his file as an academic integrity concern.

You told me "nothing about this goes on Owen's file." Now it's an integrity concern in his file. Your own procedure, 4.4, says a first concern means a supervised reassessment and nothing in the record, and if you put this on his file I'm going to the principal today.
So we're agreed: a supervised rewrite, and a note on file.
No. We're not agreed on anything, Hale. A note on his file is the one thing I will not sign, and I haven't seen your documents yet.
